mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a > 0.25% increase in FEDFUNDS, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a > 0.5% increase in UNRATE, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances following two consecutive quarters of GDPC1 decline, or if the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets anticipate improved economic conditions.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances following a > 2% increase in INDPRO, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4%) suggests a tight labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to strong consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances when UNRATE is below 4%, or if the correlation between low UNRATE and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) suggests a shift in consumer spending from goods to housing, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as markets anticipate a housing boom.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances following the described interaction, or if the correlation between the interaction and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where during a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 2%), a decrease in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% within a month signals easing inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real rates improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances following the described interaction during a tightening cycle, or if the correlation between the interaction and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of industrial production (INDPRO > 105) suggests strong economic activity, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to robust corporate earnings and economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances when INDPRO is above 105, or if the correlation between high INDPRO and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
